questions.q: What is the usual shape of an input tensor for a sequence model?
why: Correct: batch first, then time, then features.

questions.q: Series length 500, input 48, horizon 24, stride 1. How many windows?
Same series, but stride 24. How many windows? (A window starts at 0, 24, 48 ... and must fit fully.)
questions.why: Window starts are 0, 24, ..., up to the last start 500 − 72 = 428. 428 // 24 = 17, so starts 0 to 17 steps: 17 + 1 = 18.

questions.q: Which statement about sliding_window_view is true?
options: It copies each window into new memory.
It returns a view; writing to it can change the original array.
why: Correct. Use .copy() before you modify the windows.
It works for any number of axes via the axis argument.

questions.q: Your validation score is great but live performance is poor. You shuffled windows randomly into train and validation. What happened?
options: Overlapping windows leaked future information into training.
The batch size was too large.
why: A small model would give a poor validation score too.
Correct: neighbouring windows share most values, so validation looked like training data.
Batch size does not cause this.

questions.q: You must scale features. Which is correct?
options: Compute mean/std on all data, then split.
Compute mean/std on the training part, apply to train and validation.
why: Correct: the scale is part of the model and may only use the past.
Different scales for the two parts make them not comparable.

questions.q: Window length is 10 (input 7 + horizon 3). Training windows end at index 11 (the last training window starts at 11). What is the smallest start index of a validation window with no overlap?
questions.why: The last training window covers rows 11 to 20. A validation window with no shared rows starts at 21 (that is 11 + 10, a gap of 9 windows).
